question.text: This slave who frequently had visions led a rebellion in Southampton County, Virginia after witnessing a solar eclipse in 1831.
question.clue: This leader asked, "Was not Christ crucified?" in response to being questioned if he were mistaken about the circumstances that led him to lead a march on the town of Jerusalem.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Whiskey Rebellion.
swap.text: The Whiskey Rebellion was put down by the Watermelon Army, led by "Lighthorse Harry," a member of this family. "Lighthorse Harry" was the father of a Civil War general with this surname, who surrendered at Appomattox Courthouse.
swap.clue: Another person with this surname was nicknamed "Granny" after losing the Battle of Cheat Mountain, but was later affectionately nicknamed "Marse."

question.text: This chief justice for the case wrote "a negro, whose ancestors were imported into America and sold as slaves," would never be a citizen even if freed and had no right to sue in U.S. Courts.
question.clue: After replacing William Duane, he ordered the end of federal deposits into the Second Bank of the United States as Secretary of the Treasury, but Jackson's bid to replace Gabriel Duvall with this man was a failure.

swap.text: This final commander of the Army of Northern Virginia declined to lead the Union side at the beginning of the Civil War and ultimately surrendered the Confederate Army at Appomattox Courthouse.
swap.clue: This general, whose estate was confiscated for a veterans' cemetery, captured John Brown at Harpers Ferry.

question.leadin: The 1850s were a crazy time in US history. answer these questions about that decade.
question.text: Between 1854 and 1859, "border ruffians" fought "free states" after the implementation of popular sovereignty in the namesake state of this violent conflict.
question.clue: One side in this conflict received Sharps rifles from a Brooklyn minister, which became known as "Beecher's Bibles." "Border ruffians" from a neighboring state voted illegally in an election held during this conflict.

swap.text: Jackson was accidentally shot by his own troops in this battle. Despite being outnumbered, Robert E. Lee defeated Joseph Hooker at this Virginia battle.
swap.clue: It's not Fredericksburg, but during this battle, John Sedgwick's defeat at Salem Church pushed his forces back to the Rappahannock River.

question.leadin: Name some things about trains and the Civil War.
question.text: A.P. Hill's Confederates beat back Burnside's attack and saved the day at this battle after rushing over from taking the critical railroad bridge at Harper's Ferry. The Emancipation Proclamation was announced after this battle.
question.clue: Robert E. Lee retreated across the Potomac following this battle, which gave Abraham Lincoln the political capital needed to issue the Emancipation Proclamation.

swap.text: After pro-slavery forces from Lecompton sacked the town of Lawrence, this abolitionist perpetrated the Pottawatomie Massacre in revenge. This abolitionist's most famous action was funded by the "Secret Six."
swap.clue: After the sack of Lawrence, this man orchestrated the Pottawatomie massacre, which insinuated "Bleeding Kansas".

question.text: Popular sovereignty in Utah and New Mexico was decided as part of a set of measured passed in what year by Congress?
question.clue: The Seventh of March Speech byDaniel Webster supported this legislation, and one of its components upheld so-called "Bloodhound Laws."

swap.text: A newspaper casualty list prompted Walt Whitman to serve as a nurse at this battle's site of Chatham Manor. Ambrose Burnside's disastrous retreat following this battle was known as the "Mud March".
swap.clue: Though it isn't Antietam, during the first battle at this location, Prospect Hill and the Sunken Road were key defensive points.

question.text: This 1862 act, named for a Senator from Vermont, started the tradition of agricultural and mechanical colleges around the United States, often financed with the sale of public property.
question.answerHtml: Morrill Land-Grant Act of 1862 [or Land-Grant College Act of 1862]
question.clue: Lyman Trumbull was initially asked to be the sponsor for this bill by the man sometimes given credit for its introduction, Jonathan Turner, but he instead supported a Vermont Representative as this bill's sponsor.

swap.leadin: Mike Royko coined a nickname of a politician with this last name, "Moonbeam," from his then-girlfriend Linda Ronstadt.
swap.text: Name this last name of a politician who proposed Jesse Jackson as a running mate in the 1992 presidential election. That politician with this last name served as governor of California like his father, Pat, who lost to Reagan.
swap.answerHtml: Brown [accept Jerry Brown or Edmund Gerald Brown Jr; accept Pat Brown or Edmund Gerald Brown]
swap.clue: The death of Elijah (+) Lovejoy prompted a man of this surname to state, "I consecrate my life to the destruction of slavery."

question.leadin: The Union army sought to capture Richmond, but met with strong resistance on May 5, 1864 in the first confrontation between Grant and Lee.
question.text: Identify this battle of the Civil War, so named for the dense thicket which made coordinated maneuvers difficult.
question.clue: Longstreet and A.P. Hill were dispatched to Brock road, where Longstreet was wounded by friendly fire, taking him out of action in the ensuing Battle of Spotsylvania Courthouse.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about ridges in the Civil War.
swap.text: Missionary Ridge, along with Lookout Mountain, saw the encampment of Braxton Bragg in November of 1863, but he was defeated by Grant and Sherman, lifting the siege of this city.
swap.clue: This fourth-largest city in the state borders Georgia and sits on the Tennessee River, which is dammed at Chickamauga Lake just north of this city that was immortalized in a Glenn Miller track about a train trip.

question.leadin: Name some Union commanders who were present at Gettysburg.
question.text: This man commanded the 20th Maine regiment at Gettysburg and later commanded union troops at Appomattox when the South finally surrendered. He would later become Governor of Maine.
question.clue: After being discharged from military service, this former professor of rhetoric served as the president of Bowdoin College and the Governor of his home state of Maine.

swap.text: During the Civil War, this woman earned the nickname "Angel of the Battlefield" for her work in bringing supplies to wounded soldiers at Antietam and elsewhere. This woman founded the American Red Cross in 1881.
swap.clue: On account of her friendship with Louis Appia, she lobbied the U.S. to attend the first Geneva Convention, and she read the book A Memory of Solferino.

question.leadin: After he helped destroy some bridges following the Pratt Street Riot, he was arrested at his home in Cockeysville.
question.text: Name this member of a state militia, who famously petitioned for a writ of habeas corpus.
question.clue: Among those who cut the telegraph lines was this Confederate recruiter, who was subsequently detained without habeas corpus, leading to an ignored decision by the Taney court restricting Lincoln's powers.

swap.text: Back in his Confederate days, Joe Wheeler guarded the left flank of the rebels at this 1863 battle. Union General George H. Thomas became known as the "Rock" of this battle following his successful defense.
swap.clue: By ordering his troops to stand and fight on Snodgrass Hill, George Thomas averted a complete disaster, which earned him the sobriquet "The Rock of" this battle.

question.leadin: Name these heroes of nutty post-Reconstruction southern politics.
question.text: This Senator opposed the Funding Act of 1870 in Virginia as leader of the Readjuster party, which sought a reduction in state debt. This dude, known as "Little Billy," gained fame as the hero of the "Battle of the Crater" during the siege of Petersburg.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Thomas Nast's cartoon "This Is a White Man's Government."
swap.text: The cartoon is an attack on this son of a banker, who ran against Ulysses Grant as the Democratic candidate for President in 1868.
swap.clue: This man earned the nickname "The Great Decliner" by his opponents after he declined the Democratic nomination but then wept during his acceptance speech. This New York governor was the first presidential candidate to metaphorically get the bloody shirt waved at him.
